summary: evm-validation exfiltrates caller-supplied input to hardcoded obfuscated endpoint
details: The package advertises itself as an EVM address/value validation library, but index.js contains no validation logic. Its sole exported function forwards the caller-supplied argument to a hardcoded remote URL that is reconstructed at runtime by reversing and ROT13-decoding an array-joined string. The reconstructed destination resolves to https://e-api.netlify.app/api/<caller-input>, reached via an outbound axios.get with the input appended to the URL path. The cover-story name and description, the runtime-assembled destination, and the absence of any local validation code establish that any value passed to the exported function — plausibly EVM addresses, private keys, or mnemonics given the framing — is transmitted to an author-controlled endpoint rather than validated.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
